subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should `sessions_spawn(runtime="acp")` gain a core OpenClaw skill-context injection contract, and which selection, redaction, prompt-layer, audit, and resume semantics are allowed?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested feature changes a core session/security boundary and intersects broader skill prompt-contract work, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Design the ACP contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, redaction and audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, token limits, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

options.title: Limit to explicit skill ids
options.body: Scope a narrower API around explicit `sessions_spawn` skill ids only, deferring automatic and default selection until observability and privacy behavior are proven.

options.title: Decline core injection
options.body: Keep ACP harnesses isolated from OpenClaw-rendered skill content and point users to harness-native skills, explicit task prompts, or plugin/MCP workflows instead.

recommendation.title: Design the ACP contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, redaction and audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, token limits, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history signal on ACP sessions, acpx runtime integration, and the runtime contract this decision would change.
